reasons: Classification is correct: Section 15 requires the other party's approval with only a 'financially responsible affiliate' carve-out and no reasonableness standard, so it fails the ASSIGN fallback (mutual right to assign to successors; consent not unreasonably withheld) on two material terms — no M&A/successor carve-out for Client and an absolute consent veto.

The redline is targeted and minimal: it inserts 'which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed' and a Client-side successor carve-out (merger, acquisition, reorganization, sale of substantially all assets) while preserving the existing mutual structure and affiliate carve-out; the 0.55 changed-character ratio reflects necessary insertions, not a rewrite.
The reasonableness standard applied mutually is consistent with the preferred position (Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not unreasonably withheld) and does not disadvantage us.

Comment is accurate, correctly scoped, and states what changed and why with the playbook basis; the rationale properly notes the un-pressed preferred sub-element (bar on assignment to a Client competitor) as a note rather than a separate flag, and correctly confirms no change-of-control trigger exists in the document.
Severity 'high' is appropriate; although the rationale invokes walk-away language, the absence of any Vendor change-of-control termination or re-pricing right keeps this short of critical.
